0.0.n: Combined with の, it specifies which year's event is being discussed.

0.1.n: Links 来年 to ワールドカップ, making next year describe the event.

0.2.n: This is the name of the international sporting competition, written in katakana.

0.3.n: Marks next year's World Cup as the topic; the following line says what will happen.

1.0.n: Names the starting part of the broadcast period, followed by から.

1.1.n: Marks 朝 as the starting point in time.

1.2.n: Here it refers broadly to the middle of the day, rather than precisely noon.

1.3.n: Connects 朝から昼 to 時間帯, describing the span covered by that time slot.

1.4.n: Refers to a stretch of time rather than one exact moment.

1.5.n: Marks the time period when the broadcast will happen.

1.6.n: Refers to television transmitted from ground stations, rather than satellite or cable.

1.7.n: Marks terrestrial TV as the medium used for the broadcast.

1.8.n: Polite passive form of 放送する; the World Cup receives the action, and 来年 gives it a future meaning.

1.9.n: Adds this fact as a reason supporting the speaker's wish in the next line.

2.0.n: Used with の before a noun to describe a large number.

2.1.n: Links 多く to 人; together they describe a large number of people.

2.2.n: Japanese nouns do not require a plural ending; 多く makes the plural sense clear.

2.3.n: Marks the people the speaker wants to perform the watching, not the speaker.

2.4.n: 見る becomes 見て, then adds ほしい to express a wish for someone else's action; です makes it polite.

2.5.n: Softly invites the listener to share the speaker's hope, rather than demanding an answer.

0.lit: As for next year's World Cup,
0.tip: は sets up the topic, but the sentence continues into the next line.

1.lit: During the morning-to-afternoon time slot, it will be broadcast on terrestrial TV, and,
1.tip: The ending し presents the broadcast schedule as a reason for the wish that follows.

2.lit: I want many people to watch it, right!
2.tip: Person + に + verb in て-form + ほしい expresses wanting someone else to do something.
